app-caller.title: Caller agent app
app-caller.note:
• Package the voice agent as a standalone 'Caller Agents' app, so the same engine can take or make phone and web calls outside a storefront.
• Reuse the voice server, call ending and engine. Only the entry point and settings differ.
• Done when a demo call works end to end and is ready for the landing page.

app-shopify.title: Shopify plugin: embed widget and app setup
app-shopify.note:
• Ship the Shopify app: install via OAuth, add the widget through a theme app extension, and read products and policies.
• Handle the plan tiers (Starter €99, Growth €249, Scale €499+) with Shopify billing and a 14-day trial.
• Done when it installs cleanly on a dev store and passes Shopify's app review checklist.

be-buyer.title: Buyer psychology playbook in the agent prompt
be-buyer.note:
• Write the core system prompt so the agent sells like a good in-store salesperson, not a chatbot: short, warm and helpful.
• Cover the real reasons people hesitate: shipping cost, returns, fit/size, compatibility, product differences. Use social proof, scarcity and reciprocity only when honest.
• Done when 10 test conversations on the demo store resolve the doubt in a few turns without sounding scripted.

be-callend.title: Time-aware call ending
be-callend.note:
• End calls naturally: wrap up once the doubt is solved, the shopper goes quiet, or a time limit is hit (frequency capping, as in the plan).
• Say a short goodbye, give a next step (cart or checkout), and save the outcome to the transcript.
• Done when no call hangs open and each ending is logged with a reason.

be-conf-ai.title: Confusion engine v2: grows with each customer
be-conf-ai.note:
• Stretch goal: replace the fixed thresholds with a model that learns from each store's sessions and outcomes (bought vs left).
• Uses the transcripts and events from the Learning card. Must fall back to v1 rules if confidence is low.
• Ships only if green by Oct 20; otherwise it's the first update after launch.

Note: Stretch: ships only if green by Oct 20, otherwise first update after launch.

be-conf-hard.title: Confusion engine v1: hardcoded rules
be-conf-hard.note:
• Detect hesitation from cursor and scroll with clear rules: hovering on price or shipping, back-and-forth between variants, long idle on the cart, exit-intent movement.
• Output where the hesitation is (the element) and the likely reason, so the prompt opens with the right question beside that element.
• Done when the rules fire correctly on the demo store, appear at most once per session (no pop-up spam), and are tuned against recorded sessions.

be-diar.title: Speaker detection with diarization
be-diar.note:
• Tell the shopper's voice apart from background voices and the agent's own audio (diarization plus echo cancellation).
• Ignore TV and other people talking so the agent answers only the shopper.
• Done when a noisy-room test doesn't trigger false replies.

be-eval.title: Evaluation engine: collect data, flag hallucinations
be-eval.note:
• Score every conversation automatically: was the answer grounded in the knowledge base, was the doubt solved, did the shopper buy?
• Flag hallucinations (claims not in the KB) and slow turns, and feed this into the dashboard insights for merchants.
• Done when each call gets a score, and flagged calls can be listed for review before pilots.

be-geo.title: GEO optimization: tool alignment to find the right product
be-geo.note:
• Make product search sharp: map how shoppers phrase things ("something for running in rain") to the right catalog items and variants.
• Tune tool descriptions and search so the agent picks the correct tool and product first time.
• Done when a test set of 30 shopper questions lands on the right product at least 90% of the time.

be-kb.title: Grounded knowledge base from the store catalog
be-kb.note:
• Build each store's knowledge base from its catalog, FAQ, shipping and returns pages (imported at onboarding).
• The agent may only state facts found here. Retrieval returns the source so evaluation can check it.
• Done when the demo store's catalog is indexed and answers cite the right product or policy.

be-learn.title: Learning: capture call transcripts and collect data
be-learn.note:
• Store transcripts, hesitation events and outcomes (purchase or not) per session, with consent and EU storage.
• This data powers the merchant dashboard (where and why shoppers hesitate), the A/B tests in the pilots, and v2 engines later.
• Done when every demo session leaves a complete, queryable record and opt-out deletes it.

be-onb.title: Onboarding setup fix: save store config and catalog import
be-onb.note:
• Fix onboarding saves: a new store's settings (voice, persona, language, trigger sensitivity) and catalog import must persist reliably.
• Import from Shopify first, then Shopware/WooCommerce. Re-sync when products change.
• Done when a fresh store goes from install to a working agent in about 5 minutes, as ivay.tech promises.

be-prof-ai.title: Customer profiling v2: updates dynamically
be-prof-ai.note:
• Stretch goal: update the profile during the call from what the shopper says and how they react, not just their cursor.
• Feed changes back to tone and recommendations in real time.
• Ships only if green by Oct 20.

Note: Stretch: ships only if green by Oct 20.

be-prof-hard.title: Customer profiling v1: a few hardcoded behaviors
be-prof-hard.note:
• Tag each shopper with a simple profile from behaviour: excited, hesitant, comparing, price-sensitive, or frustrated.
• The profile picks the tone and the psychology moves. Keep it session-only unless the shopper consents.
• Done when the tag is produced live on the demo store and visibly changes how the agent opens.

be-reco.title: Inventory recommendation system
be-reco.note:
• Stretch goal: suggest alternatives or add-ons from the catalog when an item is out of stock or the shopper is unsure.
• A simple catalog-based version is fine for launch. Insights for merchants' inventory can come later.
• Ships only if green by Oct 20.

Note: Stretch: a simple catalog-based version is fine for launch.

be-reverse.title: Reverse seller psychology moves
be-reverse.note:
• Add the 'reverse seller' moves: gentle, low-pressure lines such as "this might not be the right one if…" that build trust rather than push.
• Trigger them only for hesitant or sceptical profiles. Never invent stock levels or fake urgency.
• Done when they're in the prompt with examples and switch on by profile tag.

be-tone.title: Tone and persona (matches the avatar personality)
be-tone.note:
• Define Ivay's persona and voice: enthusiastic with excited buyers, reassuring with hesitant ones, solution-focused with frustrated ones.
• Match it to the avatar's look so voice and visuals feel like one character, and pick TTS voices to suit (DE + EN).
• Done when the persona doc is agreed with Saleeta and wired into the prompt with per-mood tone rules.

Note: Agree the persona with Saleeta so voice and avatar feel like one character.

be-tools.title: Agent tool calling: product lookup, cart, handoff
be-tools.note:
• Give the agent tools: product lookup, variant/size info, shipping and returns policy, add to cart, and hand off to a human or email.
• Tools read the store's own catalog and policies through the API, so answers are grounded in real data and never guessed.
• Done when the agent can find a product, answer a shipping question and add an item to the demo cart in one call.

dep-api.title: API server (router): auth, routing, sessions
dep-api.note:
• Build the central API router: merchant auth (Shopify/Shopware app keys), shopper session IDs, and routing to voice, engine and tools.
• The storefront widget talks only to this server. Add rate limits, CORS for store domains, and request logging with session IDs.
• Done when the widget on the demo store can start a session, keep it alive and close it cleanly.

dep-db.title: Databases: sessions, customer profiles, transcripts, catalog
dep-db.note:
• Set up storage for sessions, shopper profiles (hesitation signals, mood), call transcripts and each store's product catalog.
• Keep every table scoped to a store ID so one merchant never sees another's data. Store personal data only with consent, and add a retention/delete path.
• Done when migrations run on staging and prod and the API server can read and write every table.

dep-engine.title: Deploy backend engine (confusion + profiling) as a service
dep-engine.note:
• Package the confusion engine (hesitation detection) and customer profiling as one service behind the API server.
• It takes cursor, scroll and click events from the widget and returns 'intervene now / where / why' plus a profile tag.
• Done when it runs on staging, handles several sessions at once, and responds fast enough not to delay the prompt.

dep-host.title: Pick hosting (AWS or custom) and provision staging + prod
dep-host.note:
• Pick where Ivay runs for launch: the plan pilots on the team's own hardware first, then moves to elastic cloud. Data must stay in the EU (GDPR).
• Provision staging and prod with the same setup (containers, env vars, secrets, TLS, domain under ivay.tech).
• Done when both environments are reachable, documented in the repo, and cost per month is written down.

Note: Decide on day 1. Almost everything downstream waits on this card.

dep-tokens.title: Token tracking: per-call usage and cost logging
dep-tokens.note:
• Log tokens, audio minutes and cost for every call, tagged by store and session.
• The plan budgets about €0.05–0.10 LLM cost per conversation, so this is how we check margins on the €99/€249/€499 tiers.
• Done when a per-store daily cost total can be queried and an alert fires if one call goes far over budget.

dep-voice.title: Voice agent server / voice API running end to end
dep-voice.note:
• Run the voice pipeline end to end: mic in, speech-to-text, LLM reply, text-to-speech out, on self-hosted open models where possible.
• Target from the business plan: first audio back in under 200 ms after the shopper stops talking. German and English voices.
• Done when a shopper on the demo store can hold a natural two-way voice conversation with no manual steps.

Note: Push to talk, diarization, call ending and the caller app all wait on this.

fe-avatar.title: Avatar personality: look, idle and speaking states
fe-avatar.note:
• Design Ivay's avatar: a friendly look with idle, listening and speaking animations that stay light enough not to slow the store page.
• It should feel like the persona (agree it with Zain) and sit politely beside the product, not cover it.
• Done when the states are wired to the voice events and the bundle stays small.

Note: Agree the persona with Zain (tone card).

fe-forms.title: Onboarding forms design
fe-forms.note:
• Design the merchant onboarding screens: connect store, pick voice and persona, language, how sensitive the triggers are, and consent text.
• Keep it to a few steps. Ivay.tech promises setup in about 5 minutes with no credit card for the 14-day trial.
• Done when the designs are ready to build and include empty, error and success states.

fe-mode.title: Chat or voice button
fe-mode.note:
• Design the small, quiet invitation that appears next to the element causing hesitation, with a clear choice: talk (voice) or type (chat).
• No pop-up that blocks the page, and easy to dismiss. Shoppers who dismiss it shouldn't see it again that session.
• Done when it works on desktop and mobile on the demo store and matches the avatar style.

fe-onb.title: Onboarding workflow end to end
fe-onb.note:
• Build the onboarding flow from the designs and connect it to the backend save and catalog import.
• Finish with a 'test it on your store' preview so the merchant hears the agent before going live.
• Done when a new merchant completes onboarding without help and the widget shows on their store.

fe-presets.title: Chat presets (very minimal)
fe-presets.note:
• Add 3–4 one-tap starter questions in chat mode, such as "Shipping cost?", "Which size?" and "Return policy?".
• Pick them from the hesitation reason the engine sends, so they fit the moment.
• Done when presets change with context and tapping one starts the right answer.

fe-ptt.title: Push to talk
fe-ptt.note:
• Build push-to-talk for voice mode: hold or tap to speak, with clear listening, thinking and speaking states.
• Handle mic permission prompts gracefully and fall back to chat if the mic is blocked.
• Done when it works in Chrome, Safari and mobile browsers on the demo store with the live voice server.

mk-acq.title: Client acquisition: sign 10 design-partner stores
mk-acq.note:
• Sign design-partner stores: a free pilot in exchange for data and a case study. Fechtklingen.de and RetailMeOff.de come first.
• Get a written pilot agreement or letter of intent from each store.
• Done when 10 stores have agreed and have a start date.

mk-browser.title: Use-case story: Browser agents
mk-browser.note:
• After launch: a use-case story on Ivay as a voice layer for browser agents.
• A short page or post with one demo.
• Pick it up only if design partners ask for it.

Note: After launch. Pick the next one based on what design partners ask for.

mk-caller.title: Caller Agents: landing page and demo call
mk-caller.note:
• Build a landing page for Caller Agents with a live demo call button.
• Explain the use case simply and capture leads into HubSpot.
• Done when the page is live and the demo call works.

mk-cold.title: Cold calling: script and first 50 calls
mk-cold.note:
• Write the call script from the interview guide: problem, how they handle it now, reaction to Ivay, willingness to pilot.
• Make the first 50 calls to the scraped list and document every conversation.
• Done when the calls are logged and objections are summarised for the pitch.

mk-gwy.title: Use-case story: Grow-with-you agents
mk-gwy.note:
• After launch: a use-case story on agents that grow with each customer.
• A short page or post with one demo.
• Pick it up only if design partners ask for it.

Note: After launch. Pick the next one based on what design partners ask for.

mk-hubspot.title: HubSpot: pipeline, lead stages, capture form
mk-hubspot.note:
• Set up HubSpot: pipeline stages (contacted, talked, pilot, paying), a lead capture form on ivay.tech, and an email sequence.
• Track the plan's first-year funnel: about 150 contacts, 30 calls, 6 pilots, 4 paying.
• Done when every lead and conversation is logged there.

mk-interview.title: Use-case story: Voice agent for interviews
mk-interview.note:
• After launch: a use-case story on the voice agent running screening interviews.
• A short page or post with one demo.
• Pick it up only if design partners ask for it.

Note: After launch. Pick the next one based on what design partners ask for.

mk-lang.title: Use-case story: Language learning
mk-lang.note:
• After launch: a use-case story on language-learning conversations.
• A short page or post with one demo.
• Pick it up only if design partners ask for it.

Note: After launch. Pick the next one based on what design partners ask for.

mk-linkedin.title: LinkedIn: company page and launch post series
mk-linkedin.note:
• Refresh the company page and plan a launch series: the problem (cart abandonment), a demo clip, the founder story, and pilot results.
• Post 2–3 times a week leading up to Oct 24.
• Done when the posts are scheduled and the page links to ivay.tech.

mk-research.title: Market research: ideal customer and competitor scan
mk-research.note:
• Define the ideal customer: Shopify/Shopware stores with €0.5–10M revenue, products that need explaining, and 20k+ product page views a month.
• Scan competitors (Hotjar and FullStory analyse but don't act; Zoovu, Heyday and Rep.ai are scripted chat) and sharpen our one-line pitch.
• Done when there's a one-page ICP and positioning doc the whole team uses.

mk-rtca.title: Use-case story: Real-time call assistant
mk-rtca.note:
• After launch: a use-case story on a real-time assistant during calls.
• A short page or post with one demo.
• Pick it up only if design partners ask for it.

Note: After launch. Pick the next one based on what design partners ask for.

mk-scrape.title: Web scraping: list of target Shopify stores
mk-scrape.note:
• Build the target list: Shopify stores that match the ideal customer, starting with Bonn, Köln and NRW, then DACH.
• Grow the existing 38-shop priority list with contact name, email, phone and store size.
• Done when 150+ qualified stores are in HubSpot.

mk-shopify.title: Shopify App Store listing: copy, screenshots, demo video
mk-shopify.note:
• Write the App Store listing: headline, benefits (more sales from existing traffic, no pop-up spam), screenshots and a 30–60 s demo video.
• Show pricing tiers and the 14-day free trial, and replace the placeholder metrics on ivay.tech with real or honest numbers.
• Done when the listing is submitted alongside the app.

mk-social.title: Use-case story: Social media bots
mk-social.note:
• After launch: a use-case story on voice bots for social media.
• A short page or post with one demo.
• Pick it up only if design partners ask for it.

Note: After launch. Pick the next one based on what design partners ask for.

qa-callend.title: Q&A: call ending
qa-callend.note:
• Test every way a call ends: doubt solved, shopper silent, time limit, shopper leaves the page, network drop.
• Check the goodbye, the next-step hint, and that the outcome is logged.
• Pass when no call stays open and every call has an ending reason.

qa-latency.title: Q&A: latency
qa-latency.note:
• Measure time from when the shopper stops speaking to the first audio back. The target in the plan is under 200 ms.
• Also measure how quickly hesitation becomes a prompt on screen. Test under several sessions at once.
• Pass when the 95th percentile meets the target on prod hardware.

qa-profiling.title: Q&A: customer profiling
qa-profiling.note:
• Act out each profile (excited, hesitant, comparing, price-sensitive, frustrated) on the demo store.
• Check that the right tag fires and that the tone and moves change to match.
• Pass when each scripted persona gets the expected tag most of the time.

qa-session.title: Q&A: session handling
qa-session.note:
• Test sessions: page reloads, several tabs, moving from product to cart, timeouts, and two shoppers on one store.
• Check that no data leaks between stores or shoppers.
• Pass when sessions survive navigation and close cleanly.

qa-tokens.title: Q&A: token tracking
qa-tokens.note:
• Check that the token and cost logs match the provider bills for a sample of calls.
• Confirm the cost per conversation sits around €0.05–0.10 as the business plan assumes, and that alerts fire.
• Pass when the totals reconcile within a small margin.

qa-tools.title: Q&A: tool calling
qa-tools.note:
• Test every tool: product lookup, variants, shipping and returns answers, add to cart, handoff.
• Use the 30-question GEO test set and check that answers match the store's real data.
• Pass with no wrong product added to a cart and no invented policy.

qa-voice.title: Q&A: voice quality
qa-voice.note:
• Test voice quality: clarity, natural pauses, interruptions (barge-in), noisy rooms, and German and English accents.
• Run on desktop and mobile, with good and bad networks.
• Log issues as cards; pass when 20 test calls sound natural with no robotic glitches.

rel-go.title: Go / no-go review and release checklist
rel-go.note:
• Go/no-go review on Oct 23: all Q&A cards passed, blockers closed, privacy (consent, opt-out, EU data) checked.
• Prepare a short release checklist: rollback plan, monitoring, on-call person, and known issues.
• Decision recorded on the board with who signed off.

rel-launch.title: Release to market
rel-launch.note:
• Release to market on Sat Oct 24: Shopify app live, ivay.tech updated, and pilot stores (Fechtklingen.de, RetailMeOff.de) switched on.
• Post the launch on LinkedIn and email the design-partner list.
• Watch errors, latency and costs closely for the first 48 hours.
